analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation-only addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 85-91). It describes how `EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate` handles out-of-order completed observations: age and expiry are anchored to the newest observation per aggregate, current-posture or workload-bucket series. Averaging and sample counts follow receipt consumption order. An older receipt cannot move freshness backward or create a false evidence gap, and a heartbeat snapshot never renews evidence. No code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior changes. The base units (4, 5) are unchanged surrounding text with no diff; head unit 6 covers only the first ~404 lines of the head, including the changed hunk. I found no security regression and no invalidated threat-model assumption. Relevant context: the described freshness semantics touch the deadline and qualified-profile telemetry path, which is performance/availability evidence and not directly a canonical threat. It relates loosely to T-010 and T-029 (availability) and to routing evidence. The doc says expiry stays anchored to the newest observation, and a heartbeat alone never renews evidence, which is consistent with the existing statements about measurement expiry. The actual implementation (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift) is not in this batch, so I cannot confirm that the code matches the doc. If later passes see a code change there, they should verify that a malicious or stale receipt cannot extend freshness for qualified deadline profiles. Head text beyond line 404 was not supplied, so the rest of the head file was not examined, but the patch excerpt is complete and shows no other changes.
